bull_bear.body:
- Diversified and innovative product portfolio spanning traditional snacks, potato chips, extruded snacks, fryums and fruit drinks, catering to consumers across all age groups (SWOT - Strengths)
- Strong focus on quality and food safety compliance, with continuous quality monitoring and process controls maintained through FY2025-26
- Technology and data driven operational governance (SWOT - Strengths)
- Experienced and committed leadership team (SWOT - Strengths)
- Own brand "Skitos" being built alongside contract manufacturing, which lets the Tumkur plant serve both branded and third-party demand
- Demonstrated process-engineering gains at the plant - a Potato Grader that improved chips quality and reduced slicer damage/breakdown, and a Vibro shaker (De-Oiling belt) delivering approximately up to 4% oil saving in pellet products
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Raw material and packaging input cost and availability volatility — Management flags that volatility in the cost and availability of raw materials and packaging inputs can affect margins, and the SWOT lists volatility in raw material prices and dependency on the availability of raw materials at competitive prices. For a potato-chips and snacks manufacturer this is the primary margin driver; mitigation is limited to procurement optimisation, vendor relationships and alternate sourcing, with no hedging or pass-through mechanism described.
- Intense competition from both organised and unorganised players, with limited product differentiation — The Company competes in a fragmented FMCG snacks market against organised and unorganised participants, and its own SWOT records limited product differentiation in certain product categories as a weakness. That combination caps pricing power for a sub-scale player competing against national snack brands.
- Dependence on third-party distributors for market penetration and reach — Listed verbatim as a weakness in the Company's SWOT. Route-to-market is not owned, so distribution expansion - the Company's stated primary growth lever for the "Skitos" brand - depends on partners the Company does not control.
- Manufacturing and supply-chain concentration at the Tumkur, Karnataka facility — The Company's manufacturing is at a single stated facility at Tumkur, Karnataka, and management flags that operational disruptions or inefficiencies in logistics and supply chain can result in delays or increased costs. Mitigation is process reliability, buffer stocks where necessary and vendor contract review; there is no second site named to absorb a disruption.
- Demand sensitivity to macroeconomic conditions and consumer spending — Management flags that fluctuations in inflation, interest rates and consumer spending patterns can impact business growth, and the SWOT names sluggish or fluctuating consumer demand patterns as a threat. Persistent inflationary pressures on input and logistics costs are cited separately as a threat, so the Company can face weak demand and rising costs at the same time.
- Increasing health consciousness shifting dietary preferences away from fried packaged snacks — Named as a threat in the SWOT. This is the structural, secular risk to the product portfolio - potato chips, fryums and extruded snacks - rather than a cyclical one, and it is the risk least addressable by cost or distribution actions.
- Regulatory and compliance risk around food safety, packaging and labelling — The SWOT names regulatory changes relating to food safety, packaging and labelling requirements as a threat, and the secretarial auditor identifies the Food Safety and Standards Act 2006, the Legal Metrology Act 2009 and the Trade Marks Act 1999 as the laws specifically applicable to the Company. Non-compliance in a food business carries product-recall and licence consequences, not just penalties.
- Technology and cybersecurity risk from increasing digitalisation — Management flags that increasing digitalisation exposes the business to cyber threats, data security risks and potential system disruptions, addressed through IT security controls, data backup, access management and periodic monitoring.

outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Ceeta discloses no new plant, no greenfield project and no capital commitment for FY2025-26 - the named Capital Commitments disclosure states that "The company does not have any capital commitments in the current and previous year." Expansion in the year was incremental debottlenecking and modernisation at the existing Tumkur, Karnataka plant, described in the Section 134(3)(m) annexure. The largest item was the installation of 2 new modernised packing machines, which increased capacity from 10 tons per day to 12 tons per day. Other plant investments included a mezzanine racking system to increase storage, an online conveyor belt enabling online packing of potato chips (controlling material spillage and reducing manpower), online metal detection for product safety, a Vibro shaker (De-Oiling belt) installed across all pellet product lines at the units, a Potato Grader, an Air turbine, and a new SS Cylinder with Solenoid Timer. Utility and environmental infrastructure added or in place includes a 10 KLD sewage treatment plant whose treated wastewater is used for gardening and flushing, a 140 KLD ETP and water recycling plant recycling roughly 80% of discharged water, rainwater harvesting at the plant, VFDs on the air compressor, Trafo power-factor correction equipment, IE3 five-star motors replacing older heavy-duty motors, LED lighting, smart thermostats and panel-wise energy and line-wise water meters; the Company also uses bio-mass briquettes to generate process heat. The Company states that capital expenditure on energy conservation equipment is not separately accounted. Forward-looking intent is framed as strengthening manufacturing capabilities and operational efficiency rather than as any named or dated project.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Indian FMCG sector grew steadily in FY 2025-26 on improving consumer sentiment, rising disposable incomes, increasing urbanisation and expanding retail penetration, aided by moderating inflation and favourable policy measures
- Food and beverages remained a key contributor to FMCG growth, driven by changing consumer lifestyles, increasing preference for packaged and branded products and rising demand for convenience foods
- The Indian snacks industry - traditional snacks, potato chips, extruded snacks, namkeens, fryums and other ready-to-eat products - continued to see strong demand across consumer segments
- Rural consumption trends improved on favourable agricultural conditions, rising rural incomes and government rural-infrastructure initiatives; urban demand stayed resilient on premiumisation and convenience-led consumption
- Growing adoption of organised retail, e-commerce and quick-commerce channels, plus rising internet penetration, digital payments and better logistics, is enhancing product accessibility and market reach
- Product innovation, new flavour offerings, improved packaging formats and greater focus on quality and food safety continued to drive industry growth
- Management cites industry estimates that the Indian FMCG market grows from approximately US$ 289 billion in 2025 to US$ 643 billion by 2030, and the Indian snacks market from approximately Rs 48,543 crore in 2025 to Rs 1,04,650 crore by 2034, a CAGR of around 8.9%
- Headwinds flagged for the industry: raw material price volatility, inflationary pressures, supply chain disruptions and intense competition
- Macro backdrop cited as supportive - India's real GDP grew 7.6% in FY 2025-26, with IMF projecting ~6.5% growth in 2026 and RBI projecting 6.9% for FY 2026-27
- Increasing adoption of technology, automation and Artificial Intelligence across manufacturing, distribution and supply chain operations is expected to enhance productivity and operational efficiency

For a potato-chips and snacks manufacturer this is the primary margin driver; mitigation is limited to procurement optimisation, vendor relationships and alternate sourcing, with no hedging or pass-through mechanism described.

risks.risk: Intense competition from both organised and unorganised players, with limited product differentiation
risks.note: The Company competes in a fragmented FMCG snacks market against organised and unorganised participants, and its own SWOT records limited product differentiation in certain product categories as a weakness. That combination caps pricing power for a sub-scale player competing against national snack brands.

risks.risk: Dependence on third-party distributors for market penetration and reach
risks.note: Listed verbatim as a weakness in the Company's SWOT. Route-to-market is not owned, so distribution expansion - the Company's stated primary growth lever for the "Skitos" brand - depends on partners the Company does not control.

risks.risk: Manufacturing and supply-chain concentration at the Tumkur, Karnataka facility
risks.note: The Company's manufacturing is at a single stated facility at Tumkur, Karnataka, and management flags that operational disruptions or inefficiencies in logistics and supply chain can result in delays or increased costs. Mitigation is process reliability, buffer stocks where necessary and vendor contract review; there is no second site named to absorb a disruption.

risks.risk: Demand sensitivity to macroeconomic conditions and consumer spending
risks.note: Management flags that fluctuations in inflation, interest rates and consumer spending patterns can impact business growth, and the SWOT names sluggish or fluctuating consumer demand patterns as a threat. Persistent inflationary pressures on input and logistics costs are cited separately as a threat, so the Company can face weak demand and rising costs at the same time.

risks.risk: Increasing health consciousness shifting dietary preferences away from fried packaged snacks
risks.note: Named as a threat in the SWOT. This is the structural, secular risk to the product portfolio - potato chips, fryums and extruded snacks - rather than a cyclical one, and it is the risk least addressable by cost or distribution actions.

risks.risk: Regulatory and compliance risk around food safety, packaging and labelling
risks.note: The SWOT names regulatory changes relating to food safety, packaging and labelling requirements as a threat, and the secretarial auditor identifies the Food Safety and Standards Act 2006, the Legal Metrology Act 2009 and the Trade Marks Act 1999 as the laws specifically applicable to the Company. Non-compliance in a food business carries product-recall and licence consequences, not just penalties.

risks.risk: Technology and cybersecurity risk from increasing digitalisation
risks.note: Management flags that increasing digitalisation exposes the business to cyber threats, data security risks and potential system disruptions, addressed through IT security controls, data backup, access management and periodic monitoring.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Ceeta Industries Limited, founded in 1984, is a diversified enterprise that has repositioned itself around FMCG, manufacturing packaged traditional and extruded snacks under its "Skitos" brand from a single plant at Tumkur, Karnataka.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company manufactures packaged snack foods - traditional snacks, potato chips, extruded snacks, fryums and other snack products - along with fruit drinks in various flavours, sold under its own brand "Skitos". It also undertakes contract manufacturing for third-party customers, leveraging its manufacturing expertise and operational capacity. Products are positioned as quality offerings at competitive price points and reach consumers through a distributor-led network across multiple sales channels in India.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body:

- Vaibhav Heavy Vehicles Ltd. — related party: Enterprise under common control; dealings comprise reimbursement of expenses with an opening and closing balance
- Tetron Commercial Ltd. — related party: Enterprise under common control; the Company's borrowing counterparty - loan borrowed and repaid with interest during the year, and provider of a corporate guarantee to Canara Bank on behalf of the Company
- Tetron Capital Ltd. — related party: Enterprise under common control; named in the related-party list, no transaction line shown in the routed extract
- Nouveau Metal Industries Ltd. — related party: Enterprise under common control; named in the related-party list, no transaction line shown in the routed extract
- Rashmi Properties & Investments Ltd. — related party: Enterprise under common control; dealings comprise reimbursement of expenses

- Kingstone Krystals Ltd. — related party: Enterprise under common control; reimbursement of expenses paid on the Company's behalf
- Coronation Refrigeration Industries Ltd. — related party: Enterprise under common control; landlord for premises at Bangalore - security deposit against rent paid and rent paid, with a closing rent payable balance
- Mindstream Agrico Private Limited — related party: Enterprise under common control; named in the related-party list, no transaction line shown in the routed extract
- Impact Corporate Investments Pvt. Ltd. — related party: Enterprise under common control; named in the related-party list, no transaction line shown in the routed extract
- Balaji Infra & Logistics Private Limited — related party: Enterprise under common control; named in the related-party list, no transaction line shown in the routed extract

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Packaged snacks:** Skitos, Traditional snacks, Potato chips, Extruded snacks, Fryums
- **Beverages:** Fruit drinks (various flavours)
- **Contract manufacturing:** Contract manufacturing for various customers

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Indian FMCG / packaged snacks consumers (urban and rural)
- Organised retail, e-commerce and quick-commerce channels
- Third-party brand owners via contract manufacturing
- Domestic only - the Company had no foreign exchange earnings or outgo in FY2025-26 or FY2024-25

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Indian FMCG sector grew steadily in FY 2025-26 on improving consumer sentiment, rising disposable incomes, increasing urbanisation and expanding retail penetration, aided by moderating inflation and favourable policy measures
- Food and beverages remained a key contributor to FMCG growth, driven by changing consumer lifestyles, increasing preference for packaged and branded products and rising demand for convenience foods
- The Indian snacks industry - traditional snacks, potato chips, extruded snacks, namkeens, fryums and other ready-to-eat products - continued to see strong demand across consumer segments
- Rural consumption trends improved on favourable agricultural conditions, rising rural incomes and government rural-infrastructure initiatives; urban demand stayed resilient on premiumisation and convenience-led consumption
- Growing adoption of organised retail, e-commerce and quick-commerce channels, plus rising internet penetration, digital payments and better logistics, is enhancing product accessibility and market reach
- Product innovation, new flavour offerings, improved packaging formats and greater focus on quality and food safety continued to drive industry growth
- Management cites industry estimates that the Indian FMCG market grows from approximately US$ 289 billion in 2025 to US$ 643 billion by 2030, and the Indian snacks market from approximately Rs 48,543 crore in 2025 to Rs 1,04,650 crore by 2034, a CAGR of around 8.9%
- Headwinds flagged for the industry: raw material price volatility, inflationary pressures, supply chain disruptions and intense competition
- Macro backdrop cited as supportive - India's real GDP grew 7.6% in FY 2025-26, with IMF projecting ~6.5% growth in 2026 and RBI projecting 6.9% for FY 2026-27
- Increasing adoption of technology, automation and Artificial Intelligence across manufacturing, distribution and supply chain operations is expected to enhance productivity and operational efficiency

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Expand the distribution network across both existing and new markets to widen reach for the packaged snacks portfolio
- Strengthen the visibility and equity of the Company's own brand "Skitos"
- Enhance operational excellence through prudent cost management across production, sales, distribution and administrative functions
- Continue focusing on operational efficiency and cost optimisation to strengthen business operations
- Deploy surplus funds strategically into short-term investment opportunities to optimise returns
- Conserve resources rather than pay dividend, to fund future expansion and strategic investments

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Ceeta discloses no new plant, no greenfield project and no capital commitment for FY2025-26 - the named Capital Commitments disclosure states that "The company does not have any capital commitments in the current and previous year." Expansion in the year was incremental debottlenecking and modernisation at the existing Tumkur, Karnataka plant, described in the Section 134(3)(m) annexure. The largest item was the installation of 2 new modernised packing machines, which increased capacity from 10 tons per day to 12 tons per day. Other plant investments included a mezzanine racking system to increase storage, an online conveyor belt enabling online packing of potato chips (controlling material spillage and reducing manpower), online metal detection for product safety, a Vibro shaker (De-Oiling belt) installed across all pellet product lines at the units, a Potato Grader, an Air turbine, and a new SS Cylinder with Solenoid Timer. Utility and environmental infrastructure added or in place includes a 10 KLD sewage treatment plant whose treated wastewater is used for gardening and flushing, a 140 KLD ETP and water recycling plant recycling roughly 80% of discharged water, rainwater harvesting at the plant, VFDs on the air compressor, Trafo power-factor correction equipment, IE3 five-star motors replacing older heavy-duty motors, LED lighting, smart thermostats and panel-wise energy and line-wise water meters; the Company also uses bio-mass briquettes to generate process heat. The Company states that capital expenditure on energy conservation equipment is not separately accounted. Forward-looking intent is framed as strengthening manufacturing capabilities and operational efficiency rather than as any named or dated project.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Diversified and innovative product portfolio spanning traditional snacks, potato chips, extruded snacks, fryums and fruit drinks, catering to consumers across all age groups (SWOT - Strengths)
- Strong focus on quality and food safety compliance, with continuous quality monitoring and process controls maintained through FY2025-26
- Technology and data driven operational governance (SWOT - Strengths)
- Experienced and committed leadership team (SWOT - Strengths)
- Own brand "Skitos" being built alongside contract manufacturing, which lets the Tumkur plant serve both branded and third-party demand
- Demonstrated process-engineering gains at the plant - a Potato Grader that improved chips quality and reduced slicer damage/breakdown, and a Vibro shaker (De-Oiling belt) delivering approximately up to 4% oil saving in pellet products
